summary: Per-frame suspension and wheel physics tick (proposed name from existing analysis; ABI lead is a generic Wheel_Contact_Force_Integration name, LEGACY). Loop 1 walks the four 1124-byte wheel blocks starting at this+1040: resolves each wheel's suspension geometry base, transforms anchor offsets through the car body (this+0x141C) and wheel-hub (this+0x15F0) rotation matrices via Matrix3x3VectorMultiply, builds and normalizes the suspension direction, computes cross-product torque terms from both transforms, and applies ConstraintEnforce per wheel. Then, when dword_7CE958 (tire model mode) is set, accumulates scaled force contributions into four torque accumulators. Two anti-roll-bar blocks (front, gated by bypass bytes this+1164/this+2288; rear, gated by this+3412/this+4536) compute torque deltas from damper-load differences and optionally add half of a PiecewiseFunctionEval correction. Loop 2 walks the same wheel blocks from this+1004, scales the stored direction triple by the block force double and feeds it to AccumulateAngularMomentum and F_3DVectorSubtractWithCrossProduct. Returns 0. Called per frame by PhysicsIntegrationStep (00441d60).

operations.description: Iterate over the four wheel suspension blocks: block base at this+1040 (byte offset 0x410), stride 1124, loop counter from 4 down to 1
Within each block, process only when the flag byte at block offset 124 is zero (wheel 0 flag byte at this+1164); a non-zero flag skips the block
Resolve the suspension geometry base pointer: dword at block offset -36, defaulting to the pointer stored at this+1287 (dword index, byte offset 0x141C) when it is null
Matrix3x3VectorMultiply(geometry base+28, block vector, out): rotate the suspension anchor offset into world space
Build the first world-space point by adding the body transform rows (base+4, base+12, base+20 of the pointer at this+0x141C) to the rotated offsets
Matrix3x3VectorMultiply(second transform+28, block vector, out): second world-space rotation using the pointer at this+1404 (dword index, byte offset 0x15F0)
Build the wheel-hub world-space point by adding the second transform rows (base+4, base+12, base+20 of the pointer at this+0x15F0) to the rotated offsets

Subtract the two world points (wheel-offset components at this+0x410, this+0x418, this+0x438, this+0x440, this+0x448), compute the length with sqrt and normalize the difference into a unit direction vector
Read the two global double constants dbl_59E420 and dbl_59E880 used in the normalization/scaling arithmetic (exact operator mapping not visible in the decompiled text)
Store the normalized direction triple into the per-wheel accumulator buffer (v41, advancing 24 bytes per wheel)

Compute suspension torque terms from the body rotation rows (base+124, base+132, base+140) against the wheel offsets, combined with the translation rows (base+100, base+108, base+116) of the pointer at this+0x141C
Build the matching torque terms from the second transform rows (base+124, base+132, base+140 plus base+100, base+108, base+116) of the pointer at this+0x15F0
Subtract the two torque vectors and combine the difference with the normalized direction (dot product) to form the suspension force scalar
ConstraintEnforce(block state at block offset -388, distance, force scalar): apply the suspension constraint force for this wheel
If dword_7CE958 (tire model mode) is non-zero, accumulate angular contributions from the second transform direction

Accumulate the scaled squared-length of the second transform rows (base+100/+108/+116) times the scale fields this+0x1448 / this+0x1450 into the four accumulators this+0x490, this+2292 (front) and this+0xD58, this+4540 (rear)
Front anti-roll block: process only when both bypass bytes this+1164 and this+2288 are zero
Front anti-roll torque delta = (this+1140 - this+1156 - (this+0x8D8 - this+0x8E8)) scaled by this+0x1438; accumulate into this+0x490 and this+2292 with opposite signs
If the byte at this+5216 is non-zero, add half of PiecewiseFunctionEval evaluated on (this+0x8D8 + this+1140)/2 and (this+0x8E0 + this+1148)/2 to both front accumulators
Rear anti-roll block: process only when both bypass bytes this+3412 and this+4536 are zero
Rear anti-roll torque delta = (this+3388 - this+3404 - (this+0x11A0 - this+0x11B0)) scaled by this+0x1440; accumulate into this+0xD58 and this+4540 with opposite signs
If the byte at this+5216 is non-zero, add half of PiecewiseFunctionEval evaluated on (this+0x11A0 + this+3388)/2 and (this+0x11A8 + this+3396)/2 to both rear accumulators

Second pass over the four wheel blocks starting at this+1004 with stride 1124: skip each block whose byte at block offset 160 is non-zero (flags this+1164, this+2288, this+3412, this+4536 for wheels 0..3)
Scale the stored per-wheel direction triple by the double at block offset 164 (wheel 0 at this+0x490; other wheels at this+2292, this+3416, this+4540)
AccumulateAngularMomentum(block state at block offset 28, scaled triple): add the wheel angular momentum contribution to the vehicle
F_3DVectorSubtractWithCrossProduct(block state at block offset 76, scaled triple): subtract the force and add the cross-product torque (wheel 0 state at this+0x438)
Return 0 (loop counter reaches zero) as the per-frame result; invoked per frame by PhysicsIntegrationStep (00441d60)
